metadata.Status / priority: HISTORICAL PUBLIC DATA; medium for retrospective technology-spending accountability.
metadata.Publisher / coverage: U.S. General Services Administration; federal award and indefinite-delivery vehicle data, including orders, modifications and Other Transaction records as documented. Structured data, not a library of signed contract PDFs.
metadata.Documentation / evidence: https://open.gsa.gov/api/contract-awards/ ; attached Contract Awards PDF pp. 2–7; live page checked 2026-09-23.
metadata.Access and cost: free public/revealed data with SAM personal API key. Default ordinary non-federal account with no SAM role: 10 requests/day; documented role-associated personal account: 1,000/day. Higher limits require actual eligibility, not an invented affiliation.
metadata.Scale: default 10, maximum 100 records/page; search caps at first 400,000 records. Asynchronous format=csv or format=json extracts cap at 1,000,000. Narrow date/agency partitions and verify completeness; download/status requests can consume additional quota. Do not assume an extract is one unlimited call.
metadata.Timing and restricted fields: contracts both funded and awarded by Defense enter the revealed tier when signed at least 90 days earlier; civilian-funded or civilian-awarded records are treated differently. Immediate-parent and domestic-parent names and entity identifiers are excluded from the revealed response. Do not promise an ownership graph from public fields.
metadata.Useful joins: Procurement Instrument Identifier (PIID), agency, referenced vehicle identifier, modification/transaction identifiers, solicitation ID, awardee Unique Entity ID, Commercial and Government Entity code, places and dates. PIID alone can be ambiguous.
metadata.Methods: distinguish transaction dollarsObligated from totalDollarsObligated; inspect modifications and descriptions; compare competition and number of offers where supplied. piidAggregation summarises award families and related orders; do not add those totals to their components. deletedStatus retrieves deleted contracts within the documented six-month window; deletion can be correction, not concealment.
metadata.Reporting value: growth beyond launch coverage, changes in beneficiary, concentrated suppliers, a change in location or purpose. Source disclosure delay must be included in historical news comparisons.
metadata.Evidence: https://open.gsa.gov/api/itcollect/ ; attached PDF pp. 1–2; live page checked 2026-09-23.
metadata.Contents: public exclusions, including documented supply-chain security orders. Search response is paginated, default 10 records; first 10,000 cap. Extract route up to 1,000,000 records. Ordinary non-federal no-role account: 10 requests/day.
metadata.Access / scale: personal key for public tier; paginated search default 10 records and first 10,000 cap; extract route offers CSV/JSON up to first 1,000,000. See endpoint-specific role limits before collection.
metadata.History: search provides latest active version; documentation directs historical-version users to Data Services. Active notices updated daily, archived weekly. Archive our own observations; do not assume a current attachment existed on the original posting date.
metadata.Joins / reporting: notice ID, solicitation number, agency, dates, named places and award details when present. Study terms of reference, planned base support or closures, unusual research questions and sole-source explanations. No minimum dollar threshold for this lane. Download public attachments separately and respect their individual access restrictions; this public search is not the restricted Opportunity Management interface.
metadata.Contents / joins: documents, comments, dockets and available attachments; document ID, docket ID, agency and dates. Request attachments explicitly on detail calls; they are not included by default. Partition large comment retrievals to respect the documented pagination ceiling.
metadata.Reporting value / limits: resolve recipients, track name/address/registration changes, support exclusions matching. Not an unrestricted beneficial-ownership register. Public-display opt-outs and controlled hierarchy/contact fields create gaps; sensitive financial and tax identifiers are not public data.
metadata.Joins / method: resolve entity identifiers where present plus names, addresses, excluding agency, classification and effective/termination dates. Match eligibility at the relevant award date and read the exclusion's scope; similar names or a current exclusion do not establish an unlawful earlier award.
metadata.Limits: only qualifying sites with minimum 50 visits in the reporting period; sampling and participation gaps. Not individual visitor tracking, a census of public interest, or a measure of newspaper coverage. Avoid treating the analytics-version break as a real change in demand.
metadata.Contents / cadence: monthly public entity files cover active entities and those expired within six months; daily public exclusions files cover active exclusions; separate daily supply-chain order extracts are documented. Daily entity deltas described in this PDF are controlled/sensitive, not a promised public feed.
metadata.Method / limits: cache public snapshots for repeated local matching. A current active-only exclusions file cannot establish historical eligibility; keep dated snapshots or seek suitable historical records. Inspect file-date conventions and coverage before treating absence as a change.
metadata.Contents / access: active/inactive assistance programme descriptions, eligibility, objectives and financial context; personal key, ordinary no-role account 10/day, maximum 1,000/page.
metadata.Use: understand distinctions among dates, obligations, potential values, competition and modification reasons in legacy records. Field names/definitions must be checked against the actual version returned now. The filename version is not evidence of freshness.
metadata.Use / limits: seed agency website monitoring and identify persistent losses of public access. Save repeated observations: one failed scan or redirect is not proof of censorship, disappearance of a programme, or closure of an agency.
metadata.What this upload proves: the logged-in interface lists contract-award dictionaries and specifications, including Atom and multiple FPDS versions. It does not itself establish that any particular bulk data export is available or complete.
metadata.Useful fields: agency/contract identifier, modification and transaction numbers, signed/effective dates, reason for modification, description of requirement, extent competed and number of offers. The document includes award, vehicle and Other Transaction examples.
metadata.Potential value: compare reported subcontracting goals and actuals, if records become available through authorised disclosure.
metadata.Access: API.data.gov key for read requests; separate activation requirements apply to posting comments, which is outside this collection workflow.
metadata.Function / access: submission, updates and deletion of reports by authorised reporting entities; system account, reporting permissions, registered IP and testing requirements. Listed retrieval operations do not imply unrestricted public reporting data. Use public acquisition/assistance subaward read APIs instead.
metadata.Decision: consider only with an authorised affiliate arrangement; it does not supply a general replacement for GDELT or the pilot's independent coverage search. Do not reuse credentials exposed by unrelated sites.
metadata.Access / limits: documentation requires a valid federal government system account key and limits use to validating locations submitted to SAM. SAM is not an authoritative gazetteer.
metadata.Reporting questions: which companies seek exemptions or changes, what evidence underpins a rule, and what consequences are buried in supporting reports? Link claims to original submissions. Comment counts do not measure public opinion; repeated campaigns and agency-controlled field visibility complicate interpretation. A missing comment/attachment can reflect publication processing or restrictions.
metadata.Access / freshness: documentation says no user credentials/authentication; daily overnight refresh. Legacy v2 rates API retired February 2025; do not build against it.
metadata.Joins / use: vendor, contract number, labor category, worksite, education, experience, clearance and current price. Compare like-for-like published labor ceilings and changes in schedules.
metadata.Critical limit: ceiling rates are not wages, actual invoice rates or proof of overcharging. Match job requirements and contract terms before drawing comparisons.
metadata.Access / contents: public key route to historical government-wide information-technology portfolio data; documentation links to the full API specification.
metadata.Contents / use: high-level shared-service traffic and adoption totals. API use is not a count of unique people or evidence of military activity. Several field descriptions appear copied incorrectly in the document; verify returned schema before quantitative use.
metadata.Access / function: ordinary API key AND admin authentication token; administrative operations and agency analytics. Public documentation is not public data access. Metrics endpoint above is the public alternative for aggregate service statistics.
metadata.Function: POST click events for an affiliate search experience. It does not let journalists download users' search/click histories. Do not send synthetic events while testing collection.
metadata.Reason: page says no APIs are available and documents TBD responses, while also claiming v4.0 is available. Do not promote the nominal endpoint to a working source without a successful authorised response or clarified official documentation.
metadata.Potential use: procurement discovery if a public implementation is verified later; presently use the website as a pointer only.
metadata.Critical correction: agencies are no longer required to report through IT Collect. Do not treat it as a dependable current investment or AI-spending feed. Test actual coverage/end dates before comparisons and do not infer that missing updates mean cancelled investments.
